config.score_field: RQ1 signals reported side by side, no composite as headline: addie_median (LEAD — instructional-design content quality, the construct the research question is about), trajectory_score (process conformance), total_score (= 0.7*ADDIE + 0.3*Traj, ISD-Agent-Bench's own composite, kept for comparability). All from comparison_report.json, per scenario.
config.pooling: mean across runs per (model, agent, scenario)
config.rq2_failure_policies: complete_case (primary) + zero; RQ2 has no min_score policy because the alignment endpoints already floor at 0.0

comparisons.holm_family: 2 comparisons (alignmentgraph-isd vs each baseline) within model size 'qwen3.5-0.8b'; Holm applied per (signal, policy).
2 comparisons (alignmentgraph-isd vs each baseline) within model size 'qwen3.5-4b'; Holm applied per (signal, policy).

interaction.definition: DiD on addie_median = mean over scenarios of [delta(largest size) - delta(smallest size)], delta = proposed - baseline per scenario (mean of runs, complete-case); bootstrap CI (10k, seed 42) resamples scenarios; positive DiD means the proposed method's advantage GROWS with model size, negative means it shrinks (i.e. the method helps small models more).

addie_median.definition: DiD on addie_median = mean over scenarios of [delta(largest size) - delta(smallest size)], delta = proposed - baseline per scenario (mean of runs, complete-case); bootstrap CI (10k, seed 42) resamples scenarios; positive DiD means the proposed method's advantage GROWS with model size, negative means it shrinks (i.e. the method helps small models more).

failure_rates.definition: Scenario-level failure = agent missing a scorable output in >=1 of the size's runs (n_scenarios_any_missing). Fisher exact two-sided, Holm over 2 comparisons per size. Run-level counts descriptive only.

alignment.source: alignment_scores.json per scenario dir (pooled mean across runs, then across scenarios)

stats.definition: A PANEL of 6 signals, no primary endpoint and no composite: per_model[].panel[<signal>] carries the same layers for every signal, reported win or lose. Continuous signals are mean-max RECTIFIED cosine (max(0,cos) on [0,1]; no matching threshold). 'comparisons' = paired diffs (proposed - baseline) per scenario (mean of runs where scored; scenarios scored for both agents), Wilcoxon two-sided (exact null for n<=25), bootstrap CI (10000, seed 42). Multiplicity is reported twice: p_holm = Holm within one signal (2 comparisons), p_holm_panel = Holm over the whole panel x baseline family for that size. align_descriptive = per-agent mean + bootstrap 95% CI over per-scenario values. Both are COMPLETE-CASE over available outputs, not unconditional: an agent run that crashed leaves no output to score. align_failures counts those cells and comparisons_failure_zero re-runs the paired test with them imputed at 0.0 (the signal's floor; a min-score policy is degenerate here because the observed minimum IS 0.0). conditional_align = over scenarios whose output yielded >=1 objective in every scored run (isolates signal quality from parse failure). interaction_align = method x model-size DiD on the paired delta of objective_assessment_similarity (complete-case).

interaction_align.definition: DiD on the paired objective_assessment_similarity delta (proposed - baseline): value at the largest size (qwen3.5-4b) minus the smallest (qwen3.5-0.8b), per scenario; negative = the gap narrows as the model grows (i.e. widens toward small models). Bootstrap CI (10000, seed 42) + Wilcoxon p on the per-scenario DiD values.

token_usage.source: *_trajectory.json metadata (token_usage + execution_time), pooled mean across runs then scenarios; operational metadata only
